Match a profile against a profile formula

Source: R/sequence-engine.R
match_horizon_sequence.Rd

Three-valued match of the identified horizons of a profile against the profile formula of a type (the Russian Field Guide of 2008 names its types by such formulas: "O-EL-BEL-BT-C"). Generic: the codes, the vocabulary and the surface horizons are the caller's.

Usage

match_horizon_sequence(
  table,
  spec,
  vocabulary = NULL,
  surface = NULL,
  agro = NULL,
  closure_surface = FALSE,
  max_cover_cm = 40,
  max_gap_cm = 0,
  pair_gaps_cm = NULL,
  buried_within_cm = Inf,
  max_completions = 2000L,
  ...
)

Arguments

table

The identified horizons: the frame of identify_horizons, any data frame with a code column (and optionally horizon_idx, top_cm, bottom_cm, passed, candidates, features, features_na, overlay, small, transitional, buried, rockflag, mark, composition), or a character vector of codes from the top (NA an undecided layer, "" no diagnostic horizon). Rows are read in depth order when every top is recorded, else as given.

spec

The formula: a string, or one parsed by the package's parser.

vocabulary

Codes the match is closed on; NULL closes it on the formula's own codes only.

surface, agro

Natural and agro surface codes for the thickest-horizon rule; both NULL: no rule, the first horizon is the surface.

closure_surface

Whether surface and agro codes of the vocabulary that the formula does not name count in the closure (default FALSE).

max_cover_cm

Thickness of cover above which no surface run is read.

max_gap_cm, pair_gaps_cm

The gap allowed between two consecutive horizons (cm), and named allowances for pairs.

buried_within_cm

Depth within which a buried profile counts.

max_completions

Most completions of undecided layers tried; beyond it the result is NA.

...

When `spec` is a string, the arguments of the parser: test_terminals (rock and parent slots to test, by code, by signature such as "C~~" or "DG", or by text such as "[ABC]"; TRUE for all), optional (codes whose slots are optional), required_features (features required wherever written), alternatives (a named list of codes accepted in place of a written one, list(BCA = "CAT")), masters and features (vocabularies: an unknown token is then an error), parents, rock_flags and flag_masters. An error when `spec` is already parsed.

Value

A list: passed (TRUE, FALSE or NA), formula, specificity, distance and distance_exact (the edit distance of the closest reading, 0 for a match: exact when no layer is undecided, else a lower bound over the completions), matched (a data frame of slots and the horizons that fill them), missing (slots not filled), extra (horizons in play not matched), absent (optional slots not present), ignored (horizons left out of the match), surface and absorbed (the surface horizon and the ones read as its features), sequence (the codes in play), undecided (layers whose completion leaves it NA) and notes.

Details

The profile side is collapsed top-down: small horizons and transitional rows are dropped; consecutive rows with the same code are merged (sub-horizons: BT1, BT2 = BT), also across horizons left out of the match; the rows of a buried profile become one buried token. A horizon fills a slot by its code or by an overlay (an AU with an S overlay fills an S slot). With `surface` and `agro` codes, the surface slot is read by the thickest-horizon rule: the agro horizon if the surface run has one, else the thickest natural horizon starting at the surface or under a cover thinner than `max_cover_cm` (rows with no diagnostic horizon, and horizons neither in play nor surface horizons, such as litter coded L); the other horizons of that run are read as features and leave the sequence.

The match is closed on `vocabulary` (the codes of every scheme of a division): a horizon of the vocabulary, or of a tested slot of the formula, present in the profile must be matched by a slot, in order; a horizon foreign to both is ignored. Surface and agro codes the formula does not name are left out of the closure unless `closure_surface` is TRUE. Optional slots (in parentheses) may be absent. A rock or parent slot not tested (C, D, R unless flagged) takes its horizon when that code is in play and is left out otherwise. Two horizons matched one after the other must lie directly one under the other: rows with no diagnostic horizon between them may sum to `max_gap_cm`, or to the allowance of the pair in `pair_gaps_cm`, named "UPPER>LOWER" by codes (a buried profile is "[ABC]": c("AU>BCA" = 15, "RY>[ABC]" = 10)).

A layer whose code is undecided (NA, with or without a list of candidates) is completed in every way that matters: TRUE when every completion matches, FALSE when none does, NA otherwise. A required feature, rock flag or rock mark listed in features_na, a turbated composition not recorded, or an unknown thickness, leave the result NA when they decide it. More than three undecided layers with no candidates leave the result NA unless no completion can match.

Examples

# a profile as its sequence of horizon codes, from the top
match_horizon_sequence(c("AY", "EL", "BEL", "BT", "C"), "AY-EL-BEL-BT-C")$passed
#> [1] TRUE
# an optional remnant (in parentheses) absent; typical g features not needed
match_horizon_sequence(c("P", "BEL", "BT", "G", "C"), "P-(ELg)-BELg-BTg-G-CG")$passed
#> [1] TRUE
# closed on a vocabulary: a G horizon the formula does not name blocks it
match_horizon_sequence(c("O", "EL", "BEL", "BT", "G", "C"), "O-EL-BEL-BT-C",
                       vocabulary = c("O", "EL", "BEL", "BT", "G"))$passed
#> [1] FALSE
# an undecided layer that could be EL or another horizon
match_horizon_sequence(c("AY", NA, "BT", "C"), "AY-EL-BT-C")$passed
#> [1] NA
# a rock symbol tested where it names the type
match_horizon_sequence(c("O", "C", "R"), "O-(C)-R", test_terminals = "R")$passed
#> [1] TRUE
